Mitchell carries Natal separately: its `natal` label has nine items 1852-1909 (maize, tobacco, livestock) and NO sugar cane, and its `cape of good hope` label has tobacco only, so the pre-Union cane series exists only under `south africa`, the label every other pre-1910 item routes to the Cape through. The series runs straight into the Union's across 1910 (21,000 ha at 1907 -> 26,000 ha at 1910; 79,000 t at 1909 -> 72,000 t at 1910), and the Union's cane is Natal's. No collision: `natal` has no sugar-cane cell in any year, so nothing is double counted.

Period rows (year null, 1934-1938) are taken because the whole period lies inside the rule. Measured with fao52audit/ussr.py on consolidated_layer_b.parquet, 2026-09-24.

PRESENT BOUNDARIES. fao1952's 1937 USSR `population total` is 188,656 thousand. The Soviet census of January 1939 counted about 170.6 million on the pre-annexation boundary, and 1937 is two years earlier; the Baltic states, eastern Poland, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina and the Finnish cession added some 20 million. The figure is therefore the post-war territory, as the rye series is (see the `rye` rule), and the four 1937 population indicators (total, agricultural, agricultural occupied, female agricultural) share one column. Relabelled to `USSR present boundaries` -> back_cast F228-1945-1991; the pre-war horse, flax and linseed rows keep the `USSR` label and F228-1921-1940.
